title: Embeddings SDK: iterator surface and deterministic error model for Python & TypeScript
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Background: Customers using embeddings + reranking report brittle client behavior around pagination cursors, opaque retry semantics, and a mismatch between the Python and TypeScript SDK surfaces. This ticket proposes a unified iterator/streaming API for embeddings that: 1) exposes a deterministic error model (typed errors for pagination, rate limit, and partial responses), 2) supports resumable iterators with stable cursors across languages, and 3) reduces client-perceived latency by allowing streaming token-level partial embeddings and batch finalization for reranking use-cases.

Scope: Implement new iterator/streaming surface in both Python and TypeScript SDKs, update pagination semantics to use a stable opaque cursor string, add typed error classes and error codes in both runtimes, and wire up integration tests and benchmarks. No server-side protocol changes are required; this is purely client-side surface and retry semantics with feature flags for staged rollout.

Goals: 
- Provide a single high-level iterator API (async iterator in TS, iterator/async generator in Py) for embeddings results across pages and streaming chunks.
- Ensure deterministic behavior under partial failures: clearly document which errors are retryable and provide methods to resume using the stable cursor.
- Keep P50/P95 client latency for a typical 512-token batch under current SLOs while improving tail latencies under load.
- Reduce developer friction migrating from current paginated calls with ad-hoc cursors.

Non-goals: Remove server-side pagination or change tokenization. Not adding new batching heuristics; follow Optimize suggestions in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Python and TypeScript SDKs implement the new iterator surface and exported typed error classes
Integration tests covering pagination resume semantics and partial failures pass in CI
Benchmarks show no >10% regression in P50 latency for common embeddings workloads and <20% regression at P99
Documentation and migration guide published in the SDK repos and Developer Docs
Feature gated rollout completed (feature flag toggles) and canary usage on internal services succeeds for 48h
updates: 2025-03-03: Initial design spike completed. Chose async generator + IteratorProtocol to match idiomatic usage in each language. Prototype repo created: https://github.com/redwood/emb-sdk-iterator-proto
2025-03-05: Eng sync — decided on stable opaque cursor format (base64 of {v,offset,checksum}) so server compatibility is retained if we change structure later.

2025-03-07: Implemented TypeScript prototype with typed error classes (EmbPaginationError, EmbRateLimitedError, EmbPartialResultError). Local bench shows 5% improved perceived latency due to streaming first-chunk emit.
2025-03-10: Python implementation skeleton pushed (draft PR). Need to align retry policy config objects between runtimes. Assigned to Lucas for API finalization.
2025-03-11: Design review feedback from PM (Ava Chen): add explicit backpressure controls on the iterator consumer (max_buffer_size) and document memory/perf tradeoffs.
2025-03-12: Draft migration guide and example snippets added to docs branch. Starting integration test authoring.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Consumers may rely on current opaque cursor semantics and expect server-generated offsets; changing resume semantics could break some clients. Mitigation: keep cursor format forward-compatible, support a compatibility mode that mirrors current behavior behind a feature flag, and provide a migration script. Risk: memory blow-up if consumers buffer streaming chunks; mitigation: expose max_buffer_size and strongly document backpressure patterns.
migration_notes: Provide clear before/after examples in the migration guide. Offer a one-line feature-flagged opt-in for teams to test the new iterator. Provide a small compatibility helper function to translate old cursor values into the new opaque cursor wrapper during the transitional period.
qa_plan: Unit tests for typed error construction and classification
Integration tests simulating partial network failures and resume from cursor
Load test with 1k concurrent iterator consumers to observe memory and P99 latency
Canary rollout to internal service (search-rr) for 48h with automated rollback if error rate increases >2x
